svg.title: Japan at a Glance — Editorial Infographic
svg.desc: A static infographic covering Japan’s geography, economy, population, and places to visit.

text.tspan: Japan stretches along the Pacific rim of East Asia, uniting
four main islands—Hokkaido, Honshu, Shikoku, and
Kyushu—plus thousands of smaller ones. Dense cities
sit beside forested mountains, hot springs, and a coastline
shaped by both typhoons and tectonic energy.
Despite limited natural resources and a mountainous terrain that leaves only a fraction of land arable, Japan built one of the world’s most advanced
economies—anchored in manufacturing, technology, finance, and culture. High life expectancy, world-class infrastructure, and a deep continuity of tradition
sit alongside demographic headwinds and a long period of low growth, making Japan a study in resilience as much as refinement.
Measured in current US dollars,
Japan’s nominal GDP peaked near
$5.1 trillion in 2019 before easing—
shaped by yen valuation, global
demand, and domestic price dynamics.
The chart at right shows annual
nominal GDP (current US$ trillions)
from 2015 through 2024. Note that
dollar figures move with both real
output and exchange rates.

svg.text: Peak year highlighted in soft rose · Values in current US$ trillions
Ethnic / nationality grouping · approx. share of residents

text.tspan: Bars for minority groups are scaled
up for readability (not 1:1 with 97.5%).
A first trip can sample both neon megacities and quiet
shrines. These six destinations form a classic circuit:

g.text: Neon districts, museums, and endless neighborhoods
Temples, gardens, and preserved historic streets
Street food capital with castle and lively canals
Peace Memorial and the floating torii of Itsukushima
Iconic peak, onsen towns, and lake views
Wide landscapes, seafood, and powder-snow winters

svg.text: Sources: World Bank / national accounts (nominal GDP, current US$); population composition approximate from official statistics & secondary summaries (rounded).
Map is stylized for editorial layout and is not a navigational chart. Infographic designed as a single static SVG · Japan at a glance
